doc.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Professional start and leaving New Orleans
title: Joining Lee Collins and David Jones at the Astoria Ballroom
summary: Collins hired Barker for his shoes, replacing Emmanuel Sayles on banjo in the Jones and Collins Astoria Stompers, who played weekends at the Astoria across from the Pelican.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Wiggins. A great piano player. Played with him. And I played with Lee Collins and them. That’s where I graduate to big time. I joined Lee Collins and David Jones’s band. I taken [Emmanuel] Sayles’s place. They had scanned banjo players around there.

That’s why they called me to the rehearsal they had. Lee Collins look at me. I had on these $20 [? (inaudible)] shoes [? (inaudible)]. Later on he said, “You know why I hired you?” He said, “You wasn’t playing much banjo. I hired you because you had on them pretty shoes. I used to like to look at them shoes, and I knew you’d amount to something some day.” That’s why he hired me in the band. I went in the band and that’s where I heard some [expletive deleted]. Me, Roy . . . now who the hell was on bass?
With Lee Collins?
Jones and Collins Astoria Stompers.
Lee Collins played trumpet. David Jones played drums?
David Jones was a great saxophone player.
Ok. Yeah, yeah, yeah. But he also . . . Didn’t he teach music and play . . .
He probably did.
. . . a lot of instruments. That’s right. Good saxophone player. Who else was in that band?
Roy Evans on banjo. That’s all . . . Roy Evans on guitar. Who’s on there on bass? Can’t think. Theodore, David Jones were the reed section.
Theodore Purnell?
Yeah. Lee Collins on trumpet. Roy Evans on bass [sic: guitar]. I was on banjo. Joe Robichaux was on piano. I forget who was on bass.
What kind of places did you all play?
We had a steady gig, weekends on the Astoria Ballroom at Rampart and Gravier
[streets].
Astoria Ballroom on Rampart and Gravier. Was that . . .
[? (inaudible)] the Pelican Ballroom.
The Pelican?
Yeah, and Astoria was across the street.
The Astoria was across the street from the Pelican?

That’s right. They had one for uptown people, the Pelican. Downtown people was at Astoria. All the pimps and the whores used to come in the after[noon] . . . Good food in there. Good quick lunch. Sandwiches. Oyster sandwiches. All creole concoctions. It was a great experience, because I got a little recognition.
Met a lot of people that would come . . .
Yeah. People come to see David Jones. Come to see Lee Collins. Lee Collins had had a battle with Kid Rena. Blew Kid Rena off, so that meant he was the king around here for a while.
